L97: # numpy.from_dlpack【85†#】
L98: 
L99: numpy.from_dlpack(x, /, *, device=None, copy=None)【86†#】
L100: 
L101: 
L102: Create a NumPy array from an object implementing the `__dlpack__` protocol. Generally, the returned NumPy array is a view of the input object. See 【87†[1]】 and 【88†[2]】 for more details.
L103: 
L104: Parameters:
L105: 
L106: 
L107: x object
L108: 
L109: 
L110: A Python object that implements the `__dlpack__` and `__dlpack_device__` methods.
L111: 
L112: device device, optional
L113: Device on which to place the created array. Default: `None`. Must be `"cpu"` if passed which may allow importing an array that is not already CPU available.
L114: 
L115: copy bool, optional
L116: Boolean indicating whether or not to copy the input. If `True`, the copy will be made. If `False`, the function will never copy, and will raise `BufferError` in case a copy is deemed necessary. Passing it requests a copy from the exporter who may or may not implement the capability. If `None`, the function will reuse the existing memory buffer if possible and copy otherwise. Default: `None`.
L117: 
L118: Returns:
L119: 
L120: 
L121: out ndarray
L122:
